chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Safwan, from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār, from Saʿīd al-Aʿraj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: 'A man marries a woman who is not trustworthy, and she claims pregnancy.' He said: 'Let him be patient, due to the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): The child belongs to the bed (the husband), and for the adulterer is the stone.'

key_terms.وَلِلْعَاهِرِ الْحَجَرُ: and for the adulterer is the stone (penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a wife claims pregnancy but her paternity is in doubt?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the foundational legal principle of *al-waladu lil-firāsh* (the child belongs to the bed), where paternity is presumed to follow the marital bed unless specific evidence of adultery (*hadd al-zina*) is presented. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises the husband to exercise patience (*sabr*) in cases of uncertainty regarding the wife's trustworthiness, highlighting the Shia juristic preference for preserving lineage and marital stability over immediate disavowal. This ruling underscores the high burden of proof required to attribute a child to an adulterer, distinguishing between mere suspicion and established illicit relations.
